samples.summary: `bin entrypoint` tests assert on source text, not behavior; one assertion is vacuous
samples.evidence: The `bin entrypoint` describe (test/output.test.ts:303-318) `readFileSync`s src/bin.ts and string-matches it. `expect(source).toContain('outputError')` is satisfied by the import on bin.ts:13 (and by the word inside the comment on bin.ts:33) regardless of whether the catch handler calls it — it passes even if the catch body were `{}`. `expect(source).toMatch(/\.catch\(/)` matches any `.catch(` anywhere in the file, on any promise. Likewise `toContain('program.parseAsync(')` / `not.toMatch(/program\.parse\s*\(/)` pass for aliased calls (`const p = program; p.parse()`) or a `parseAsync(...)` whose promise is never awaited/handled. The claimed behavior — a rejection escaping an action handler is turned into the `{ error: { code, message } }` envelope with exit 1 — is never executed, so these two tests are presented as coverage of bin.ts but cannot fail if that behavior breaks.

samples.summary: No behavioral test for the new `parseAsync().catch(outputError)` entrypoint path
samples.evidence: bin.ts:35-37 is the new behavior (unhandled action rejection → error envelope + exitCode 1). The only test touching it is the source-string describe at test/output.test.ts:303. I searched packages/cli/test for any import or execution of bin.ts (grep for 'bin', 'parseAsync', 'spawn', 'execFile' across packages/cli/test) and found only the readFileSync source check; no test registers a command whose action rejects outside its own try/catch and asserts the envelope/exit code. A test could register a throwing action on a program and await `parseAsync().catch(outputError)`-equivalent wiring, or exercise a real command whose failure path escapes the handler (e.g. getConfig/getClient throwing before the try).
searchedFor: grep for parseAsync/spawn in test dir via output.test.ts inspection

samples.summary: Regression guard covers only docs/sheets call sites, though its comment claims it covers all of them
samples.evidence: The comment at test/output.test.ts:174-180 states "Reintroducing suppression at any of these call sites fails these tests." The guard only builds `registerDocsCommand` and `registerSheetsCommand` (buildProgram, lines 233-238). The diff also removed quiet-gating at call sites in notes.ts, slides.ts, api-keys.ts, tabs.ts, schema.ts and sheets-import.ts; re-adding a `if (opts.quiet) return;` there (or restoring a third argument) would not fail any test in this suite. The shared `output`/`outputError` no longer takes `quiet`, so per-command regressions are exactly what needs guarding, and the comment overstates the coverage.
searchedFor: grep 'quiet' in packages/cli/test (only output.test.ts drives commands)

samples.summary: The stdin branch of the newly try-wrapped `cells batch` input read is untested
samples.evidence: cells.ts moved both the `--data` parse and the stdin read+parse inside the try. Only the `--data '{'` path is exercised (test/output.test.ts:284-295). No test feeds malformed JSON or a failing stream via stdin (I grepped packages/cli/test for 'stdin' and found no test stubbing process.stdin for the batch command), so the half of the change that covers 'a failed stdin read' — explicitly called out in the diff's own comment — has no coverage.

samples.summary: `stubFetch` over-mocks the HTTP layer, so response handling is asserted against a hand-shaped stub
samples.evidence: stubFetch (lines 223-231) returns `{ ok, status, json }` only — no headers, no text(), no statusText. The `--quiet` guards therefore assert stdout/stderr for a synthetic client response; if the real client changes how it derives `ok`/`data` (e.g. reads headers or text for non-JSON), the tests keep passing. Acceptable for a quiet-flag guard, but it means the tests validate the formatter wiring rather than the client's response path, and the error case (500 → 'HTTP 500') is entirely determined by the stub's `status` field.

finding.summary: `bin entrypoint` tests assert on source text, not behavior; one assertion is vacuous
finding.evidence: The `bin entrypoint` describe (test/output.test.ts:303-318) `readFileSync`s src/bin.ts and string-matches it. `expect(source).toContain('outputError')` is satisfied by the import on bin.ts:13 (and by the word inside the comment on bin.ts:33) regardless of whether the catch handler calls it — it passes even if the catch body were `{}`. `expect(source).toMatch(/\.catch\(/)` matches any `.catch(` anywhere in the file, on any promise. verdict.reason: Verified in the repo. test/output.test.ts:303-318 readFileSyncs src/bin.ts and asserts only on source text. The assertion toContain('outputError') (line 316) is already satisfied by the import at bin.ts:13 and by the identifier appearing in the comment at bin.ts:33, so it passes even if the catch body were emptied; toMatch(/\.catch\(/) (line 315) matches any .catch( anywhere in the file. Neither test executes the entrypoint, so the advertised behavior (a rejection escaping an action handler becoming the { error: { code, message } } envelope with exitCode 1, bin.ts:35-37) cannot fail these tests. A repo-wide grep confirms no test imports src/bin.ts as a module or spawns dist/bin.js; the only parseAsync in tests is a locally built program at output.test.ts:241, which has no .catch wrapper under test. This is fake coverage presented as a regression guard (see comment at lines 298-302), squarely in the test-adequacy lane and major by impact.

I searched packages/cli/test for any import or execution of bin.ts (grep for 'bin', 'parseAsync', 'spawn', 'execFile' across packages/cli/test) and found only the readFileSync source check; no test registers a command whose action rejects outside its own try/catch and asserts the envelope/exit code. searchedFor: grep for parseAsync/spawn in test dir via output.test.ts inspection

verdict.reason: The new entrypoint behavior at packages/cli/src/bin.ts:35-37 (`program.parseAsync().catch((e) => outputError(e))`) has no behavioral test. The only test naming it, packages/cli/test/output.test.ts:303-318, reads bin.ts with readFileSync and asserts the source string contains 'program.parseAsync(', '.catch(' and 'outputError' — assertions that hold regardless of whether the catch emits the `{error:{code,message}}` envelope or sets process.exitCode=1; they would still pass if the catch body were a no-op. The nearby --quiet tests (output.test.ts:233-295) do call parseAsync, but on a program built in-test whose errors are all handled by each command's own try/catch (e.g. cells.ts:115-147 now wraps JSON.parse inside the try, so the malformed `--data '{'` case at line 284 never rejects out of the action), so they never reach the entrypoint's catch branch. I searched wider than the reviewer: vitest.config.ts:5 limits the suite to packages/cli/test/**/*.test.ts and I enumerated all 22 files there; grepped every CLI test for `.action(`/`new Command`/`createProgram` (only namespaces.test.ts and version.test.ts, both structure-only); and grepped the whole repo excluding node_modules for parseAsync/bin.ts/dist/bin/spawn/spawnSync/execFileSync/execa — the only executions of the built binary are the review harness (.trusted/scripts/agent/hunt-probe.mjs) and a manual debug script (packages/cli/scripts/debug-cmd.mjs:15), neither part of the test suite. No counterexample found. Under the test-adequacy rubric this is a behavior change shipped with a source-string grep presented as coverage: major.
